title: Concatenate names from nested tuples
description:
Change the following list of lists to a list of concatenated strings:

```py
names = [[('Asabeneh', 'Yetayeh')], [('David', 'Smith')], [('Donald', 'Trump')], [('Bill', 'Gates')]]
output
['Asabeneh Yetaeyeh', 'David Smith', 'Donald Trump', 'Bill Gates']
```

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `concatenate_names(names)`, returning a list of strings, one per `(first, last)` tuple found in the nested input, each formatted as `"first last"` separated by a single space.
hints: Use a nested list comprehension: an outer `for` over the one-item groups, and an inner unpacking of the `(first, last)` tuple.
Build each string with an f-string or by joining, keeping a single space between first and last name.
The comprehension shape is `[f"{first} {last}" for group in names for (first, last) in group]`.
expected_behavior: Returns a list of strings, one per (first, last) tuple in the nested input, each being the first and last name joined by a single space.
solution:
def concatenate_names(names):
    return [f"{first} {last}" for group in names for (first, last) in group]
explanation: The nested comprehension unpacks each `(first, last)` tuple from its one-item group and formats it as a single string with an f-string, collecting one concatenated name per tuple into the resulting list.
